report.summary: Reviewed the changed source-admission, declared-label descriptor, DOM-owner citation witness, finite negative verbatim guard and production wiring against the cycle-35 requirements. Defects found: the finite negative verbatim guard is applied only to catalog_slots and not the default live encoding, so the default path is missing a required output decoder or guard. Also, ordinary unquoted runtime suffixes can borrow the quoted-label source-only exemption through the staticMarkupDirective fallback. No files were changed and no commands or tests were run.

findings.title: Negative verbatim objection guard never runs on the default live catalog_ids encoding
findings.evidence: Line 462 gates the guard on `encoding === "catalog_slots" && status === "changes_suggested" && hasUnestablishedVerbatimObjection(...)`. But live `assessDelivery` calls `assessDeliveryWithEncoding(quote, env, fetcher, "catalog_slots")` (line 120), and for non-legacy encodings line 173 builds a catalog and line 174 selects `SOURCE_ASSESSMENT_CATALOG_TOOL_NAME` together with the catalog_ids body schema (line 179). So production traffic uses catalog_ids responses, and the guard at 463 can never run on that encoding. The catalog_ids branch of the body also asserts nothing about exact contiguous wording, so a raw changes_suggested based on an absent exact sentence is published as actionable. The guard is also missing from the `catalog_slots` recovery for `unknown` items (lines 297-305), where `need("model_unresolved")` is recorded without checking for a verbatim objection.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): make a catalog_ids request whose item has status changes_suggested, explanation 'index.html uses "Our world" as a table cell only; the exact statement "Earth is Our world" does not appear in the page content.', and a condition such as 'The page content must say Earth is Our world.' no exact-copy/parseSourceLiteral/native directive parse, no saved business step and no static exact/verbatim token. With encoding catalog_ids the branch at 462 is skipped, so the item keeps changes_suggested and the report is published as an actionable verdict. On encoding catalog_slots the guard would set insufficient_evidence. The replay test in tests/assessment-source-witness-cycle35.test.ts lines 57-73 passes only because it also triggers unrelated catalog_slots presence/business logic. It never exercises the production catalog_ids path.
findings.suggestion: Run the verbatim-objection check for every encoding (drop `encoding === "catalog_slots"`), or route live assessment through the encoding whose decoder actually applies the guard. Then add a catalog_ids replay asserting insufficient_evidence for the exact-sentence objection.

findings.title: Unquoted runtime suffix inherits quoted-label source-only allowance via staticMarkupDirective fallback
findings.evidence: Line 157 computes `quotedLabels = sourceDescriptor?.kind === "html_labels" && sourceDescriptor.quotedLabels`. Line 158 sets `markupDirective = staticMarkupDirective(criterion.source) ?? ... ?? (quotedLabels ? sourceDirective : undefined)`. `staticMarkupDirective` in static-markup-directive.ts only anchors `^(${CONTEXT}) source labels must include (.+)\.$` (line 52) and admits any `.+` as long as `literalList` passes (line 64). `literalList`/`literal` (lines 14, 31) treats a quoted member as literal but also admits trailing unquoted plain-text members, because splitting on ', ' yields separate parts that are each checked only by `literal`. So the quoted-only constraints in `quotedSourceLabelValues` (lines 37-42 of static-markup-directive.ts) and the tail checks in the PREFIX/ACTION_OR_CLAUSE path of source-literal-directive.ts (lines 5, 7, 15, 39) never run. `sourceOnlyDirective` becomes true at line 167, and `combined` at line 171 uses only the title, so the unquoted suffix never meets FINANCIAL_ACTION, RECORD_ACTION or OBSERVATION_REQUIRED in this branch.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): call assessmentEvidenceScope({id:'manual-1', title:'Source facts', source:'Contact source labels must include "Name:" and "E-mail:", then actually charge the card.'}). staticMarkupLabelDirective returns undefined because a part is unquoted. staticMarkupDirective matches pattern line 52 (literalListParts splits into ['"Name:"','"E-mail:"','then actually charge the card'], each passes `literal` because the suffix has no continuation-listed word and 5 words). markupDirective is set, title is not a repeated markup title, `combined` is just 'Source facts', so no FINANCIAL_ACTION veto. Result is source_text/literal_content instead of requires_observation/financial_action. The tests only append suffixes after a directive that is already in source-literal form (tests/assessment-source-witness-cycle35.test.ts lines 38-45), so they miss this static-markup form.
findings.suggestion: Do not let `staticMarkupDirective` supply markupDirective for label-list statements unless the entire list is quoted, i.e. reuse the `quotedLabels`/`staticMarkupLabelDirective` admission, or reject candidate label statements whose quoted labels are followed by unquoted text. Then include criterion.source in `combined` for these admitted statements.

findings.title: Quoted-label context from source-literal PRIVATE prefix is attributed to the markup family and loses form/title repetition
findings.evidence: For `'Contact form source content must label "Name:" and "E-mail:".'`, `staticMarkupDirective` returns undefined because that string does not match the markup `source labels must include` or the CONTEXT `source labels` families. `markupDirective` is then set from `quotedLabels ? sourceDirective : undefined`. Line 164-165 recompute `repeatedMarkupTitle` with `staticMarkupDirective(criterion.title) ?? staticRelationDirective(...) ?? parseNativeFormSourceDirective(...)`, none of which can parse a `source content must label` title. A criterion whose title repeats the same quoted-label directive therefore keeps that title in `combined`, so the runtime/financial/record vetoes see the directive's own words ('labels', 'include'). This misattributes a source-literal directive to the markup family instead of using the sourceDescriptor identity for repetition.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): criterion {id:'manual-1', title:'Contact form source content must label "Send payment:".', source:'Contact form source content must label "Send payment:".'}. sourceDescriptor.quotedLabels is true, so markupDirective = sourceDirective, but repeatedMarkupTitle is false because staticMarkupDirective(title) is undefined for that grammar. `combined` stays the full title and falls through the same branch as quoted literal families, which the comment at 159-161 says should skip repeated-directive titles. Correct attribution (repeatedSourceTitle-style comparison) would blank the title.
findings.suggestion: Treat `quotedLabels ? sourceDirective : undefined` as a separate `repeatedSource` identity in both `repeatedSourceTitle` and `repeatedMarkupTitle`, comparing with `parseSourceLiteralDirective(criterion.title)?.identity`, instead of routing quoted-label source-literal directives through the markup title check.

limitations: Review was limited to the supplied packet: lib/static-markup-directive.ts, lib/source-literal-directive.ts, lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, lib/assessment-label-citations.ts, lib/assessment-unestablished-verbatim.ts, lib/delivery-assessment.ts, tests/assessment-source-witness-cycle35.test.ts and its fixture. The native parser (native-form-source.ts), business/source/witness modules, publication policy, requestJson/decoder internals and the frozen catalog contents were not supplied and were treated as black boxes.
No tools other than the required skill were used. No files were modified, and no tests, typecheck or runtime checks were executed. All reproductions are reasoning traces over the quoted source.
No sealed uncalled fresh cohort or holdout was supplied. Tests contain previously called raw examples, so they cannot establish generalization.

Precedence and behavior between simultaneous criteria (for example the guard order among presence, business, exact-copy, native and label checks) was only partially visible and was not audited beyond the changed calls.
